About half of the tickets for "Win $50, $100 or $200" have been sold. The game is about halfway through its run. The key question is whether the tickets or the top prizes run out first. Right now, tickets and top prizes are running out at about the same rate.

Everything above about "Win $50, $100 or $200" comes from the Maryland Lottery's own published numbers. We only do the counting.
806.headline: How far along this game is

807.body:
"Ravens X2" has had no $20,000 top prize claimed for three weeks. Everyday prizes keep getting claimed, and fewer tickets are left each day. The number of tickets printed is fixed. Each day without a top prize claim leaves those prizes among fewer tickets.

Tomorrow's count on "Ravens X2" will be a little different. The game sells every day, and this page keeps track.
807.headline: Three weeks, no top prize claimed

808.body:
Of all the tickets printed for "Ravens X10", about half are still unsold. The game is in the middle of its run, with three of four top prizes unclaimed. In every scratcher, either the tickets or the prizes run out first. The rest of this page shows the details.

Every line of Ravens X10's prize table below shows today's count, not last month's.
808.headline: Early stage or late

809.body:
"Gold Bar Bingo" is about halfway through its run, with about two-thirds of its tickets still unsold. Late in a run, a game is worth a look when prizes outlast tickets. Early on, the prize design matters most. Here, the top prizes and the tickets are going at about the same pace.

Everything above about "Gold Bar Bingo" comes from the Maryland Lottery's own published numbers. We only do the counting.
809.headline: Where this game is in its run

810.body:
"In the Green" has fewer top prizes left. The count changed when one top prize of $50,000 was claimed last week. Unsold tickets still hold four of the original seven. Check the top prize count first when you compare scratchers.

If "In the Green" is your usual pick, check this page often. The prize counts change even when the ticket looks the same.
810.headline: Top prize count went down

811.body:
About a third of the tickets for "Extreme Green" have been sold. The game is about halfway through its run. The key question is whether the tickets or the top prizes run out first. Right now, tickets are selling faster than top prizes are being claimed, which is good for the tickets that are left.

Tomorrow's count on "Extreme Green" will be a little different. The game sells every day, and this page keeps track.
811.headline: How much has sold

812.body:
About a third of the tickets for "Loose Change®" are sold. The top prize count has held, with fifteen of 24 still unclaimed. The number of tickets printed is fixed, so that is a plain good sign.

If "Loose Change®" is your usual pick, check this page often. The prize counts change even when the ticket looks the same.
812.headline: Good news: no big claims

813.body:
The most common win left on "The Price is Right™" is $5. The second biggest prize left is $5,000, and eight of those are still unclaimed. The prize table is what defines a scratcher, and this page counts every level of it.

If "The Price is Right™" is your usual pick, check this page often. The prize counts change even when the ticket looks the same.
813.headline: The prize table, line by line

814.body:
"High Voltage" has gone two weeks without a top prize claim, and tickets kept selling. Only a fixed number of tickets are printed. About a third of the tickets are sold, and every remaining $100,000 prize is still unclaimed. That leaves the same top prizes among fewer tickets.

If "High Voltage" is your usual pick, check this page often. The prize counts change even when the ticket looks the same.
814.headline: No new top prize claims

815.body:
"$100,000 Crossword" is down to seven top prizes after a $100,000 winner was claimed last week. The game started with nine top prizes. Know that before you buy, because a change in top prizes changes the whole game.

Tomorrow's count on "$100,000 Crossword" will be a little different. The game sells every day, and this page keeps track.
815.headline: A top prize was just claimed

816.body:
A $50,000 top prize on "Deluxe Crossword" was claimed two weeks ago. The game started with eight top prizes and has six top prizes left. The prize table has today's count for every prize level.

If you play "Deluxe Crossword" often, bookmark this page. The write-up is updated with each morning's data.
